subject: flamingo
reasoning:
I'm planning out a flamingo model for the SDK—a single TypeScript module with a default export building the root joint, sized around 1.3m tall with standing pose, S-curved neck, pink body, and black-tipped bill as key design features.

Working through the rig structure: hip joint, leg chains with knee bends, a sphere-based ellipsoid body, tail cone, and a neck built as a swept catmull-rom curve to get that natural S-shape taper.

Head attaches at the neck tip, and I'm sketching the bill as a bent downward tube—pink near the head, darker tip—using a short swept path rather than a single straight shape to capture that distinct flamingo profile.

Now I'm working out leg placement: hip, knee, and ankle joints positioned down the body to the ground, forming a chain with named joints (hipL, kneeL, ankleL, footL) so the leg bends naturally at the right points.

For the legs themselves I'm sweeping a tapered radius along that chain and giving them a pinkish-grey color, then adding small rod-shaped toes extending forward from the foot. For the body, I'm sketching out a scaled sphere geometry to get an egg-like torso shape, adjusting the radius and scale factors since the initial numbers come out too small for the proportions I want.

Now I'm working out the wings as teardrop-shaped slabs made from a handful of points running from shoulder to tip, picking a pink-to-darker-pink color scheme and figuring out which joint should drive the wing's weighting.

Mapping out the rest of the flamingo's body: the S-curved neck built from a catmull chain with named spans, the head and bent black-tipped bill as a banded sweep, eyes as small dark spheres, and legs built as polylines with knee, ankle, and foot joints plus toe rods. I'm also sketching in wing slabs with black primary tips, a small upturned tail cone, picking out the pink and black color palette, and considering a gradient paint on the body before starting to write the actual builder code with joints, sweeps, and parts.
